_readme: Task 8, Week 1. The fixed development dataset. Owner: Person C.
This file is the source of truth for development ids. Do not invent your own ids in a test;
use these. Twenty-four documents across seven collections: 2 publishers, 2 collections,
3 institutions, 8 catalogue items, 3 entitlements, 3 admin users, 3 feed settings.
Field names mirror Person B's @Document classes as delivered in ACADEMIC.docx (13 Aug 2026),
because DemoDataSeeder binds this file to them. If a name here does not match a field there,
Jackson binds null and the seed silently writes an incomplete document, so the integration test
reads documents back and asserts values, not just counts.
DETERMINISM. Every value in this file is a literal. No timestamps are generated at load time,
no ids are random and the BCrypt hashes are pre-computed, so two developers who run this get
byte-identical databases. That is the whole point of Task 8. Do not replace anything here with
a generated value - the createdAt/updatedAt literals below stay fixed even though the real
ingest that produced these books ran at a different, real timestamp.
REAL FILES, WEEK 4. Every catalogue item here has gone through the real ingest pipeline
against the real Backblaze test-books bucket: storageKey/indexKey are real 'items/<id>/...'
objects, and masterWrappedBek (where present) is a real AES key wrapped to the master key, not
a placeholder. There is no mock/placeholder book left in this file - the eight week-1 canonical
fixtures (item_42, item_env, item_ab6, item_stat, item_dual, item_oa9, item_q7, item_f3) and the
'seed/' and 'static/mock-content/' placeholder paths they used are retired. See CONTEXT for the
cross-file cleanup this required (src/test/resources/seed/canonical-items.json,
DemoDataSeederTest, DemoDataSeederIT).
Two test scenarios lost their seed-data coverage in that cleanup and have no replacement here:
a multi-format single item (item_dual carried both a PDF and an EPUB asset; none of the eight
real books is available in two formats) and a non-READY item reaching a feed (item_q7 was
QUEUED, item_f3 was FAILED; all eight real books are READY). Whoever picks either scenario back
up should say so rather than assume it is still covered.

_notes.cipherLength: 12 (nonce) + sizeBytes + 16 (GCM tag). Null here means the asset is not encrypted, so the number does not exist. B's Asset.cipherLength is a primitive long and cannot hold null, so DemoDataSeeder maps null to 0. The null is kept in this file because 'not applicable' and 'zero bytes of ciphertext' are different facts and the validator checks the first one.
_notes.indexTerms: Same treatment. Null means there is no search index at all; B's field is a primitive int, so the mapping writes 0.
_notes.storageKeys: storageKey, indexKey and wrappedBek sit on the ITEM, not on each asset. That is B's shape, and it differs from handbook section 06, which puts them inside assets[]. Consequence: a multi-format item cannot have a per-format storage key. No item in this file currently exercises two assets - see the _readme note on lost coverage.
_notes.sizeBytes: The entity field name. The OPDS wire calls the same number originalLength.
_notes.isbn: None of the eight real books carries a scanned ISBN yet, so every item's isbn is null here.
_notes.coverKey: Real cover images, uploaded through POST .../catalogue-items/{itemId}/cover to the real bucket, for six of the eight books - the two Doctor Dolittle audio chapters have none. coverUrl stays null for all eight: the bucket is private, so a real coverUrl is never a durable literal, only a presigned link CoverUrlResolver reissues fresh from coverKey on every read.
_notes.entitlementVersion: No entitlement seeds a version. B declared 'private long version' with NO @Version annotation, so Spring Data optimistic locking is not active and the field is an ordinary number; the mapping writes 0. If B adds @Version later, 0 is still the only safe value: Spring reads a non-null version as 'this document already exists' and the first insert would fail with OptimisticLockingFailureException.
_notes.adminStatus: AdminUser.status is AdminStatus (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, DISABLED), a separate enum from RecordStatus. All three seeded admins are ACTIVE, which is valid in both, but the mapping must use AdminStatus.
_notes.adminPassword: All three hashes are BCrypt strength 10 over the development password 'wokay-local-dev'. This is a documented development credential, not a secret. It is written down so nobody has to paste it into chat. The three hashes differ because BCrypt is salted; all three verify the same password.
_notes.institutionType: ACADEMIC, not UNIVERSITY. Handbook section 06 writes 'type': 'UNIVERSITY', but B's InstitutionType has seven values and UNIVERSITY is not among them: ACADEMIC, PUBLIC, SCHOOL, SPECIAL, GOVERNMENT, RESEARCH, CORPORATE. InstitutionType.valueOf('UNIVERSITY') would throw.
_notes.feedSettings: Seeded, one per institution, because B's FeedSettings landed and week 2's shelf feeds need it. B's FeedSettingsPersistenceGuard rejects anything that is not exactly three shelves, so every row here has three, and an empty itemIds means a hidden shelf rather than an absent one.
_notes.auditLogs: Deliberately NOT seeded, although AuditLog and AuditLogRepository exist. An audit log records what actually happened; inventing entries would put fiction into the one collection whose value is that it is true. It also carries a 90-day TTL on 'at', so seeded rows would vanish and look like data loss. The admin console fills it as soon as anyone edits anything.

entitlements._seedWhy: COLLECTION scope, CONCURRENT. Covers dev-fixture-epub, the only book in col_law2024. The narrower scope, so it must beat the publisher grant below on that same book - the scope-precedence demonstration item_42/ent_imp1 originally carried.

PUBLISHER scope, UNLIMITED (copies null). Covers every Routledge book not more narrowly scoped: dev-sample-audio-encrypted, dev-fixture-pdf, item_e9a3c599, item_4062cdea. dev-fixture-epub stays under the narrower COLLECTION grant above - that is scope precedence, testable straight from the seed. validTo is null, open ended, so the seed carries one of each.

ITEM scope, CONCURRENT. dev-sample-pdf's publisher (pub_crc) has no publisher/collection-level grant to inst_7f3 - dev-sample-epub reaches it via OPEN_ACCESS instead, which this fixture deliberately isn't - so an ELITE dev fixture needs its own narrow grant rather than inheriting one meant for a different book.

feedSettings._seedWhy: The fully curated case. Three shelves, all populated, and every listed book is one Imperial can actually reach: dev-fixture-epub through the collection grant, dev-fixture-pdf and item_e9a3c599 through the publisher grant, dev-sample-epub and dev-sample-audio because open access needs no grant. itemIds order is display order and the feed must preserve it exactly.

The zero-entitlement case. UCL bought nothing, so only open access can appear, and two of the three shelves are empty. An empty itemIds is a hidden shelf, which is the OPDS 'empty shelf is omitted, not emitted as an empty array' case with real data behind it.

Leeds is SUSPENDED, so no feed is ever served for it. The record exists anyway to keep feedSettings 1:1 with institutions and to exercise the unique index on institutionId. All three shelves are empty, which is the honest content for a customer whose account is paused.
